input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: best_score calls max() over the chunk scores without a default, so an empty chunk list raises ValueError
- failure path: retrieval returns no chunks; _log_best_score calls best_score([]) before should_abstain can short-circuit; max() of an empty sequence raises and the turn crashes instead of abstaining

Reviewer finding
- description: best_score calls max() on possibly empty chunks without a guard, raising ValueError; it is now called from _log_best_score on every retrieval, including when retrieval returns no chunks.
- rationale: When self.rag.retrieve returns an empty list (a plausible case for an unmatched query), _log_best_score(chunks) calls best_score([]) which runs max() on an empty sequence and raises ValueError before the agent can reach should_abstain's empty-check. Previously should_abstain short-circuited on `not chunks`, so the empty case was handled; the new unconditional logging call makes the crash reachable on the normal path, so the question fails instead of abstaining.
critique: The finding pins down the same mechanism as the label: best_score calls max() with no default, so an empty chunk list raises ValueError. It also follows the same path, where _log_best_score calls it before should_abstain can short-circuit, so the turn crashes instead of abstaining.
